LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 9.3.1 OPPOSITES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to learn about opposites of words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the opposites of different words for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use opposites to construct sentences related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the use of opposites in communicating ideas. • Learners are guided to identify opposites from a group of words in a text. • Learners are guided to tell stories about wildlife conservation using the opposites of a variety of words, with peers. • Learners are guided to construct sentences using the opposites of words related to the theme, with peers. • Learners are guided to use opposites to respond to questions from a story, poem or a conversation. • Learners are guided to play a language game that involves identifying opposites of different words. Why is it important to learn about opposites of words? 70

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak confidently is enhanced as they construct sentences using the opposites of words.

Values:
Social justice is achieved as the learner fosters inclusivity and non-discrimination as they play language games with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is heightened as they use opposites of words in speech correctly.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner applies the knowledge on opposites to learning of similar concept in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Braille books

● Digital devices with assistive technology,

● Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

● Pictures or picture description
